steps.narration: By the end of this tutorial, you will turn a Solution Architecture Document into Terraform you can run. To start, open Deployment from the left rail.

beats.caption: Open Deployment from the left rail

steps.narration: Deployment opens on two flows. Click on DevOps, which holds the infrastructure code tools alongside the pipeline views.
Open IaC from the DevOps rail to reach the Terraform generator.

beats.caption: Open IaC from the DevOps rail

steps.narration: Two ways in from here. Connect an existing infrastructure repository from Bitbucket, or begin with an architecture document, which is what follows.

beats.caption: Existing repo, or start from a SAD

steps.narration: Step one asks where this is going. Name the project, choose a region and an environment, then supply the document.

beats.caption: Name the project, region and environment

steps.narration: Only the text is read. Diagrams in the document are ignored, so the components have to be described in words.
Upload the document or paste its text. Once it attaches, extraction becomes available.
Extraction reads the document and comes back with the infrastructure it found, grouped by kind, each one carrying what it is for.
Everything arrives selected, which makes this a starting point to generate Terraform code.
Clear the list and pick only what you need. The generate button counts what you have chosen.

beats.caption: Trim the list to what you need

steps.narration: Anything the document described but was not captured can be added by hand before you generate.
Generation writes a module for each component you kept, with root files, an example variables file and a readme.

beats.caption: A module per component, plus root files

steps.narration: Read the code before it leaves. Anything you want to change can be edited here.

beats.caption: Edit the generated code in place

steps.narration: Run the security scan and it reports what it found against the generated code, which is worth doing before anything ships.
Finally, you can download the code as a zip or push it straight to your own repository.

beats.caption: Downloaded, or pushed to your repo

steps.narration: What Velox hands over is code, not a deployment. The commands on screen are yours to run when you are ready.

variants.note: Baseline. Tutorials carry no hook or CTA.
